item.title: Atiku’s ADC owing salaries for over 12 months, APC PCC alleges
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has alleged that the African Democratic Congress ADC has not paid its staff salaries for more than 12 months, and urged Nigerians to reject the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the next general elections. In a statement on Monday in Abuja by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said it had come to its attention that the ADC National Working Committee NWC, “led by Senator David Mark as Chairman and Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola as Secretary, has refused and neglected to pay party staff for over a year.” “We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months. Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible”, APC added. The council said the development had exposed “the emptiness and insincerity of those parading themselves as ‘new saviours’.” It maintained that ADC leaders and their presidential candidate, Atiku, “do not mean well and can do nothing for our country.” According to the APC PCC, “Their desperation for power is driven by personal aggrandisement and venomous ill will against President Bola Tinubu. A party that cannot pay its cleaners and workforce cannot be entrusted with our country’s affairs.” The council also turned to Atiku’s record as an employer, saying he “has a reputation for owing his employees.” “While he regularly junkets to the UAE, staff at his Gotel Communication and other businesses also went months without pay and staged protests over unpaid salaries and other benefits,” the statement said. On Aregbesola, the council said his record “on paying workers’ salaries and pensioners in Osun State, where he was a governor for 8 years, was abysmal.” “As governor, he mismanaged the state’s finances to the point that he could not pay workers. His government thus introduced quarter-salary and, at times, half-salary payments. As for pensioners, he abandoned them for more than four years. Many died because they could not afford the basics of life”, the APC campaign added. The APC-PCC said it is therefore not surprised that ADC, harbouring birds of the same feather, cannot pay its workers’ salaries. The council then issued what it called a warning to Nigerians and working people: “reject ADC. Reject Atiku Abubakar and reject all ADC candidates in the next general elections. They do not have the interest of our country and our people at heart. “A party that aspires to govern Nigeria and which cannot be trusted with something as basic as the management of its own affairs and the welfare of its workforce should be rejected by Nigerians.” The post Atiku’s ADC owing salaries for over 12 months, APC PCC alleges appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Drop your ambition, back Tinubu, RMRDC boss tells Obi
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, has urged the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, to shelve his ambition for the 2027 election and support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Ike-Muonso, who spoke during an interactive session with reporters in Abuja, argued that the South should be allowed to complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. He said the principle of power rotation between the North and South, which has shaped Nigeria’s political calculations since the return to democracy in 1999, should guide political actors as they prepare for the 2027 general elections. “Presidential ambition must be balanced with the larger interests of national unity, political stability and the need to sustain policies that can transform the economy. Nigeria has developed a political tradition of power rotation between the North and South, and respecting that understanding can help strengthen confidence among the country’s diverse political constituencies”, he said. While he conceded that the Constitution does not prescribe a North-South rotation of the presidency, he said the arrangement has, however, remained an important consideration among major parties and stakeholders seeking to manage regional interests and maintain national balance. Ike-Muonso said Obi should consider postponing his aspiration until after Tinubu’s second term, and after the North would have the opportunity to produce a President. He said this would serve political stability, national cohesion and continuity in governance. He also urged Obi to consider joining the All Progressives Congress APC. According to him, engagement within the ruling party would let the former Anambra State governor contribute to policy debates, understand its governance structures and take part in development programmes being implemented by APC-controlled states. Ike-Muonso said membership would also give Obi a chance to observe how the party’s state governments approach infrastructure, education, healthcare, investment and economic development. He acknowledged Obi’s following, saying: “Peter Obi has built a political following and brought issues of public expenditure, accountability and economic management into the national conversation. Those issues deserve sustained engagement. But political leadership also requires strategic decisions about when to contest, when to collaborate and how best to contribute to national development.” The RMRDC chief said Obi’s influence and support base could be deployed to promote constructive engagement on governance, economic development and institutional reforms, rather than concentrating exclusively on the immediate contest for the presidency. item.title: Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria could declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as December 7, 2026, if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected following the medical evacuation of the country’s imported index patient. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, disclosed the provisional date on Monday as health authorities intensified contact tracing, investigated suspected cases and strengthened preparedness across health facilities to prevent further spread of the Bundibugyo virus disease. Writing on his X handle, Pate said the 42-day countdown towards declaring the outbreak over would be subject to validation by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and the World Health Organisation (WHO), in line with established outbreak management criteria. The development follows the evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient to Switzerland for further medical care, a move that has heightened attention on the country’s capacity to sustain containment measures and prevent community transmission. According to Pate, “Following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, our immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts and strengthened readiness across our health facilities. “If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under @WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026. This date remains provisional, subject to @NCDCgov and WHO validating the 42-day countdown. Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria,” Pate noted. He said the proposed December 7 date is therefore not a final declaration that Nigeria is Ebola-free, but a conditional target that depends on the absence of further cases and the completion of the required surveillance period. Further, he said, “Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission. “I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria.” The post Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alleged N582m fraud: Court fixes Nov 23 for trial of ex-NNPCL boss
item.description: threatens to issue bench warrant By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday fixed November 23 for the arraignment of a former President of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Abuja, Mr. Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his alleged complicity in a ₦582 million fraud. The court, presided over by Justice Lesley Wike, further threatened to issue a bench warrant against the defendant should he fail to appear before it to enter his plea to an eight-count charge preferred against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). After the case was called, the anti-graft agency drew the court’s attention to the absence of the defendant, who was billed for arraignment. According to the prosecution, the development marked the third time the defendant had stayed away from court despite being aware of the case. EFCC’s lawyer, R. U. Adagba, who informed the court that only the 2nd defendant in the matter, Abolade Nurudeen, was available for the proceedings, alleged that Ogunbayo had jumped the administrative bail granted him by the Commission. He told the court that all efforts to locate the 1st defendant for service of the charge on him had been unsuccessful. Consequently, he applied for a bench warrant to be issued to enable security agencies to arrest and produce the defendant in court for trial. The prosecution counsel premised his application for the bench warrant on the provisions of Sections 35, 113 and 114 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. However, Mr. Innocent Adoo, who announced his appearance for the defendants, opposed the application. He accused the EFCC of failing to properly serve a copy of the charge on the defendant. The defence counsel argued that arraignment in a criminal trial cannot proceed without proper service of the charge on the defendant. He submitted that a defendant must be informed of the allegations against him and given adequate opportunity to prepare his defence, adding that service could not be waived by any party. Adoo told the court that Ogunbayo was still on administrative bail and was unaware of the scheduled arraignment. He explained that the defence had used the information available to it to communicate with Ogunbayo, who was said to be in Warri, Delta State, and unable to secure a flight to Abuja for the sitting. He therefore prayed the court for an adjournment to enable both defendants to appear and take their pleas in the interest of justice. In his ruling, Justice Wike held that, in the interest of justice, the matter should be adjourned to enable the first defendant to appear for arraignment. The judge, however, warned that the court would take the necessary steps if Ogunbayo failed to appear on the next adjourned date. item.title: Man swept away by flood while trying to rescue drowning teenager in Abia
item.description: . Rescue team in desperate search for duo By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — In a heartbreaking twist of fate, a good Samaritan who risked his life to save a teenage girl from a flooded gutter in Aba, Abia State, was swept away by the same rushing water alongside the girl he tried to rescue. The tragedy occurred on Sunday evening at Ukwu Mango, Faulks Road, during a downpour, leaving residents and sympathisers scrambling desperately to find the two missing persons. The Samaritan reportedly slipped into the gutter while attempting to rescue the girl, only for the surging floodwater to sweep both of them away. Residents immediately launched a frantic search, hoping to find the pair alive, but their efforts yielded no result, fuelling fears that the victims might have been carried into the Aba River. The desperate search entered a new phase on Monday as the Abia State Fire Service and other government officials joined residents in combing the drainage channels for the missing duo. Police personnel also arrived at the scene to control the crowd and maintain order as the rescue operation continued. However, as of the time of filing this report, the victims remained missing, leaving their families and the community in agonising uncertainty over their fate. When Vanguard contacted the Police Public Relations Officer, PPRO Maureen Chinaka, she promised to revert but had yet to do so at the time of filing this report. Aba’s flat terrain makes the commercial city prone to flooding, particularly during heavy rainfall. item.title: APC accuses ADC of owing staff salaries, urges Nigerians to reject Atiku
item.description: The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) of owing its workers more than 12 months’ salaries, urging Nigerians to reject the party, its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and its candidates in the next general elections. The council’s spokesperson, Dele Alake, made the call in a statement, accusing the ADC National Working Committee, led by Senator David Mark as chairman and Rauf Aregbesola as secretary, of neglecting party workers despite their reliance on salaries for their daily needs. Alake described the alleged failure to pay the workers as “wicked and reprehensible”, questioning the party’s capacity to manage the country’s affairs if it could not meet its obligations to its own employees. “We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months,” he said. “Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible.” The APC PCC spokesperson said the allegation exposed what he described as the insincerity of the ADC leadership, adding that Nigerians should reject the party at the polls. “We have clearly stated that ADC leaders and their presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, do not mean well and can do nothing for our country,” Alake said. He further alleged that Atiku had a history of failing to pay workers, claiming that employees of Gotel Communication and other businesses linked to the former vice-president had previously gone months without salaries and staged protests over unpaid wages and other benefits. Alake also criticised Aregbesola’s record as governor of Osun State, alleging that his administration struggled to pay workers and pensioners during his eight-year tenure. He said the state government had introduced quarter-salary and, at times, half-salary payments, while pensioners allegedly went unpaid for more than four years. “We are therefore not surprised that ADC, harbouring birds of the same feather, cannot pay its workers’ salaries,” he said. Alake urged Nigerians and workers to reject the ADC, Atiku and all candidates running on the party’s platform in the next general elections. “We are sounding a warning to Nigerians and working people now: reject ADC. Reject Atiku Abubakar and reject all ADC candidates in the next general elections,” he said. He argued that a party seeking to govern Nigeria should be able to demonstrate responsible management of its own affairs and the welfare of its workforce. item.title: LAWMA begins expansion works at Olusosun dumpsite to boost waste evacuation
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, has initiated critical stabilisation and expansion works on tipping platforms E1 and E2 at the Olusosun dumpsite in Ojota. ​The upgrade, executed in partnership with Zoomlion Nigeria Limited, aims to expand platform capacity, allow more waste collection trucks to discharge simultaneously, and significantly enhance operational safety and speed. ​Speaking at the agency’s headquarters in Ijora-Olopa on Monday, LAWMA Executive Director of Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, disclosed that construction on the site is progressing according to schedule. ​Adebiyi noted that the Olusosun upgrade is part of a broader infrastructure plan that includes ongoing improvements at other major dumping facilities, such as Solus III and Epe. “Together, these upgrades are expected to strengthen the state’s overall waste evacuation network, dramatically reduce truck turnaround times, and improve service delivery across Lagos,” he stated. ​To minimise disruption during the construction phase, Adebiyi appealed for cooperation from Private Sector Participation, PSP operators, waste truck drivers, and other key industry stakeholders. ​The agency therefore reaffirmed its commitment to upgrading waste management infrastructure and maintaining a cleaner, healthier environment for all residents of Lagos State. The post LAWMA begins expansion works at Olusosun dumpsite to boost waste evacuation appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Arik Receivership: Court admits AMCON board resolutions
item.description: By Henry Ojelu The Lagos State Special Offences Court, Ikeja, on Monday admitted certified board resolutions of the Asset Management Corporation of Nigeria (AMCON) as evidence in the ongoing criminal trial of its former Managing Director, Ahmed Kuru, and others over the receivership of Arik Air Limited. Justice Mojisola Dada admitted the documents in a bench ruling, holding that they were relevant to the proceedings and duly certified in line with Section 104 of the Evidence Act, 2011. The documents were tendered by counsel to the second defendant, Mr Uyi Giwa-Osagie, to counter the claim by the fourth prosecution witness, Bawa Usman Kaltungo, that Kuru had unilaterally authorised the receivership. Kaltungo, head of the AMCON desk at the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, and leader of its investigating team, had maintained during cross-examination that Kuru, as AMCON’s managing director and chief executive officer, had unfettered powers and personally sanctioned the receivership. However, Giwa-Osagie tendered the certified board resolutions to establish that the decision was approved by AMCON’s board as a corporate body. The prosecution counsel, Dr Wahab Shittu, SAN, objected to the admissibility of the documents, arguing that they were too remote and irrelevant to the charges. But Giwa-Osagie argued that his client was not standing trial over the propriety of appointing a receiver but over other allegations contained in the charge sheet. He maintained that the documents went to the root of the case and were capable of establishing his client’s innocence. He also argued that they were public documents duly certified and tendered from the Bar. In her ruling, Justice Dada upheld their admissibility, noting that the resolutions emanated from AMCON’s board as a corporate body and had been certified in accordance with the law. The EFCC had arraigned Kuru; Kamilu Omokide, former receiver-manager of Arik Air; Captain Roy Ilegbodu, the airline’s chief executive officer; Union Bank Limited; and Super Bravo Limited over allegations arising from the airline’s receivership. The prosecution followed a petition by Mr Femi Falana, SAN, on behalf of Arik Air’s promoters and shareholders. The court adjourned the case until October 27, 2026, for continuation of trial. item.title: 2027 Polls: Don’t let politicians manipulate the law, CJN warns judges
item.description: By Ilechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja In anticipation of litigation that could arise from the 2027 general elections, the Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Monday warned judges across the country against allowing politicians to manipulate the legal system to gain undeserved advantage. The CJN particularly urged heads of courts to remain vigilant against practices capable of undermining the integrity of judicial proceedings. She identified such practices as including forum shopping, concealment of related proceedings and attempts to obtain conflicting orders from courts of coordinate jurisdiction. Speaking during the opening session of the 2026 roundtable for heads of courts, organised by the National Judicial Institute (NJI) in Abuja, the CJN said the issues called for particular attention as the nation heads towards another election season. While acknowledging that election-related disputes usually attract intense public interest and considerable pressure on the courts, the CJN said the judiciary must be prepared to discharge its constitutional responsibilities with impartiality, courage and fidelity to the law. “Political sensitivity, public sentiment or the urgency with which a matter is presented must never displace the careful application of the Constitution, the Electoral Act and the applicable rules of court. “I urge your lordships to ensure that appropriate administrative arrangements are in place to facilitate the timely and orderly handling of election-related matters. “Judicial officers must be reminded of the need to scrutinise applications carefully, insist on full and frank disclosure of relevant facts, pay due regard to related proceedings and resist any attempt to use urgent applications or ex-parte orders to secure an improper advantage. “The integrity of judicial proceedings must not be compromised by competing political interests or pressure from any quarter. “Forum shopping is particularly damaging because it undermines consistency, encourages abuse of process and exposes the Judiciary to avoidable public controversy. “Your lordships must therefore ensure that existing procedural safeguards are observed and that appropriate steps are taken whenever attempts to circumvent established judicial processes come to light. “No litigant should be permitted to manipulate the judicial system in search of a favourable decision. Public confidence in the judiciary will be tested during this period,” she added. Moreover, Justice Kekere-Ekun reminded the heads of courts that they are expected to provide the leadership necessary to ensure that election-related cases are handled competently, expeditiously and strictly in accordance with the law. She said the objective is to ensure that the courts remain impartial arbiters of disputes, free from political influence and guided solely by the facts, the applicable law and the demands of justice. item.title: ‘Atiku majored in hygiene, cannot rule Nigeria’s modern economy’ — Shettima
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Vice President Kashim Shettima has criticised former vice president Atiku Abubakar over his proposal to restore fuel subsidy, questioning his ability to govern Nigeria’s modern economy. Shettima said Atiku’s proposal would push the country back into poverty, accusing the former vice president of supporting the return of subsidy for political reasons. Speaking at the Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Monday, Shettima said, “One of the leading presidential candidates is advocating for the return of the subsidy scheme. He wants us to backslide into penury for political convenience.” He also questioned Atiku’s professional background, referring to his training at the Kano School of Hygiene as he challenged his capacity to manage the country’s economy. “I dare to put forward that his skill set — he was trained in sanitation at the Kano School of Hygiene — so he doesn’t have the skill set to govern a modern economy. That’s the painful truth,” Shettima said. Shettima further questioned Atiku’s knowledge of environmental sanitation, using the difference between flu and Ebola to make his point. “Even his decisions in environmental sanitation, I do not think he can make a distinction between flu and even Ebola,” he said. Shettima urged Nigerians to assess the proposals and qualifications of political leaders before making decisions, warning against ignoring the implications of their choices. “Nigerians must have to decide and those of you here cannot afford to play the ostrich,” he added. Atiku has advocated the restoration of fuel subsidy as part of his proposed approach to managing the economy. The issue remains a major point of disagreement between the opposition and the administration of President Bola Tinubu, which removed the subsidy in May 2023. While the government has defended the removal as necessary to reduce the financial burden on public finances, the policy has been accompanied by higher fuel prices and increased living costs for many Nigerians. item.title: Beyond spouting statistics, Peter Obi has nothing to offer — Shettima
item.description: Vice-President Kashim Shettima has criticised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, saying he has nothing to offer Nigerians beyond what he described as questionable statistics and his opposition to restoring petrol subsidy. Shettima made the remarks at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he acknowledged Obi’s position on subsidy removal but questioned the substance of his economic proposals. “I respect Peter Obi for having the courage to say he’s not going to restore the petrol subsidy, but beyond spouting some dubious statistics, Mr Peter Obi has absolutely nothing to offer,” the Vice-President said. The latest criticism marks another public attack by Shettima on Obi, whom he recently accused of relying on misleading statistics and economic prescriptions that may not suit Nigeria’s circumstances. Shettima recently questioned Obi’s comparisons between Nigeria and Bangladesh, arguing that economic policies cannot be transferred from one country to another without considering their differences. He illustrated his argument with a clothing-size analogy, saying: “He seems convinced that a size 36 shirt tailored for Bangladesh will somehow fit Nigeria’s size 52 frame.” According to Shettima, Nigeria’s economic policies must reflect its population, institutions, political environment and economic structure rather than depend on models developed for other countries. “A country of over 250 million people cannot be governed through borrowed statistics and economic prescriptions detached from its peculiarities,” he added. The Vice-President also challenged Obi’s claim that he won the 2023 presidential election, describing the assertion as unsupported by evidence. Shettima characterised the claim as a “delusion of grandeur” and criticised what he portrayed as an attempt to present old political ideas as a new direction for Nigeria. Ebola patient evacuated to Switzerland as Nigeria continues monitoring contacts Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola patient in the current regional outbreak has been medically evacuated from Abuja to Switzerland, following a significant improvement in her condition. Health Minister Muhammad Ali Pate confirmed that the patient was stable, conscious, and communicating before departure. Her husband, a Swiss diplomat who has shown no symptoms, accompanied her. The transfer does not mean the patient is no longer infectious. Strict medical precautions remain necessary, and Swiss authorities will assume responsibility for her treatment. Nigeria continues monitoring 52 other contacts. Authorities say there are currently no confirmed Ebola patients remaining in the country, although contact tracing continues. Why it matters: The evacuation changes Nigeria’s immediate case-management responsibilities, but not the need to detect possible secondary infections. The primary source of the patient’s infection also remains unresolved. Watch : Test results among contacts, the outcome of investigations into the patient’s travel history and further updates from the NCDC and Africa CDC. 2. Those identified include Peter Obi, former Senate Presidents Bukola Saraki and David Mark, and former Aviation Minister Stella Oduah. The inquiries concern alleged failures to declare offshore assets or business interests while holding public office. The investigations do not establish wrongdoing. Offshore company ownership is not inherently illegal; the relevant questions concern compliance with asset-declaration and public-office rules. item.title: Man Utd consider Howe, Nagelsmann, Conte to replace under-fire Carrick
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United are considering Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte as potential replacements for head coach Michael Carrick, whose future is in serious doubt following the club’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth, sources have told ESPN. According to ESPN, the defeat at Old Trafford on Sunday intensified pressure on Carrick, coming five days after United suffered a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League. The club have now gone eight games without a win in all competitions and sit 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone. ESPN reports that United have begun weighing up alternative managerial options, with former Newcastle United manager Howe and ex-Germany head coach Nagelsmann among the names being considered. Conte, who left Napoli in the summer, would also be open to discussions if United contacted him, the report added. United had reportedly conducted due diligence on several coaches before deciding to appoint Carrick on a two-year contract in May, following his successful interim spell. The former Manchester United midfielder is now facing an uncertain future after failing to secure a response from his players following the heavy defeat to Como. Carrick dropped captain Bruno Fernandes for the Bournemouth game after the midfielder’s criticism of the team’s approach against Como, but United delivered another disappointing performance at Old Trafford. Bournemouth scored three times through Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson, capitalising on defensive errors to deepen United’s crisis. Speaking after the defeat, Carrick said he was unsure what the club would decide about his future. “I totally understand the situation,” he said. “I am not expecting anything, I’m carrying on as normal. I love this place. I’ll always carry on doing what I think is the best for the football club.” United face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with further difficult fixtures against Aston Villa and Liverpool looming as they seek to arrest their slide. item.title: Atiku pledges gaming support after Lagos Life raises $500,000
item.description: Former vice president and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar has pledged to support Nigeria’s gaming industry following reports that Lagos Life, a Nigerian browser game, raised $500,000 in an angel investment round three days after its developer was incorporated. He made the pledge in a post on X on Monday, saying the game’s early funding success showed the potential of young Nigerian developers to build a globally competitive entertainment industry. “When a game about life in Lagos can raise half a million dollars soon after launch, our young developers are telling us something: the next global entertainment industry can be built right here,” he wrote. Atiku said he would support the sector through e-sports competitions, incentives for gaming infrastructure and financial assistance for local developers. “I will support e-sports leagues and tournaments, offer incentives for gaming infrastructure, and back Nigerian game developers with grants, incubators, and export platforms,” he said. “Our gamers are not wasting time; they are building an industry,” he added. His comments followed a report by TechCabal that Vatar Inc., the company behind Lagos Life, had secured $500,000 in an angel funding round at a valuation of $10m, three days after incorporation. The company’s co-founder and chief executive officer, Shalom Rayhamen, said that the funding round was concluded quickly because of strong investor interest in the game. “We built something people love that is growing very fast, so a lot of investors wanted to be involved,” Rayhamen said. He added, “We got the opportunity to connect and hear their offers, and because we are growing so fast, we closed it quickly so we could focus on the product.” The post Atiku pledges gaming support after Lagos Life raises $500,000 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Over 40 killed in attack on Orthodox Christians in Ethiopia
item.description: At least 43 people have been killed and 18 others wounded in an attack targeting villages, Orthodox Christian churches and homes in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, according to residents and a conflict monitoring organisation. The attack occurred on Saturday in Shirka district, about 270 kilometres south of the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa. Residents and the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data project (ACLED) reported the casualties to AFP on Monday, with local accounts suggesting that the death toll could be higher. ACLED said the attack was believed to be religiously motivated and targeted Orthodox Christians, adding that it triggered clashes with local militias that continued through Saturday afternoon and evening. A resident told AFP by telephone that the attack claimed the lives of two family members, while several relatives were reportedly taken hostage in Chole ward of Shirka district. “My sister and uncle were killed, and several of my relatives were taken hostage in Chole ward of Shirka district,” the resident said, requesting anonymity. The resident estimated the death toll at 44, while another local source put the figure at 51. A deacon from one of the affected churches said the killings had left the community devastated and called on the government to restore security. “We are deeply shocked by these tragic killings and are appealing to the government to intervene and restore security,” the deacon said, putting the death toll at 46. He added that some residents had sought refuge in nearby churches following the attack. The state-run Ethiopia Human Rights Commission said it was “following the situation” but did not provide further details. Oromia, Ethiopia’s largest region, has a population of about 40 million and has experienced a prolonged insurgency and tensions among Muslim, Protestant and Orthodox Christian communities. ACLED said attacks against Orthodox Christians in the region had increased since February 2023, with a further escalation reported since last year. It remains unclear whether the latest violence involved the Oromo Liberation Front, the main insurgent group operating in the region. Although political and ethnic representation have been central to the insurgency, religion has also been used to mobilise fighters. Ethiopia continues to grapple with several internal conflicts, including renewed heavy fighting in the northern Tigray region last month. The country’s restrictions on media access have made independent verification of reports from conflict-affected areas difficult. item.title: ‘Immigrants from shithouse country, not welcome,’ Trump blasts Norway over Nobel Peace Prize
item.description: US President Donald Trump attacked Norway during a campaign rally, calling it a “shithouse country,” and said that Norwegian immigrants were not welcome in the United States because its Nobel Committee had not awarded him the Peace Prize. “Frankly, Norway sucks. Norway has become a shithouse country, actually,” he said during Sunday’s speech. Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has made no secret of his desire to win the prestigious Nobel Peace prize. Judge and former UN rights chief Navi Pillay of South Africa was this year’s recipient. Trump has called the committee’s choice “a disgraceful and embarrassing decision” and argued that the award should have gone to him. Trump said Sunday he would welcome immigrants from certain countries but not Norway “because I didn’t get the Nobel Prize.” “So I don’t want anybody from Norway,” he said during the rally in the Michigan town of Port Huron ahead of crucial US midterm elections on November 3. There was no official indication of a new US policy on Norwegian immigrants. Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide responded to Trump’s comments about the Nobel prize on Monday, maintaining that the committee is independent. “He knows very well that the Nobel Committee is independent. We have reminded him of that, in case anyone is wondering – and that is still the case,” he told national broadcaster NRK. Trump came under fire in 2018, during his first term, after using similar vulgar expressions to refer to Haiti and certain African countries. item.title: Nigeria’s NELFUND better than US, UK education loan models – UNIBEN VC
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu, Benin City The Vice Chancellor of the University of Benin, Professor Edoba Omoregie (SAN), on Monday said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) was the best thing to ever happen to the country’s education system, arguing that the loan scheme is better than the models run by countries like the United States of America and the United Kingdom. Omoregie made this assertion in an interview with Vanguard, but, however, he said he was not impressed by the interest shown so far to access the fund. He said NELFUND was unique in every aspect, including the process of accessing it, the provision of a moratorium before repayment starts, and the percentage to be deducted when the repayment starts, saying that it was almost like a grant for education. He praised President Bola Tinubu for his quick response to the bill by signing the first one passed under President Muhammadu Buhari into law and then immediately repealing it and sending the present one as an executive bill that he said is student- and sponsors’friendly. According to him, “NELFUND is like manna from heaven; that is the way I would describe it. It is one of the most significant public policy initiatives ever introduced into this country since independence. I have to commend President Ahmed Tinubu for what he has done. He signed the NELFUND bill. There was an initial version which was developed during the time of President Buhari, but it was never signed into law. To the credit of President Tinubu, he signed the first one into law, and then when he saw that there were some operational defects, he decided to repeal and then approach the parliament to enact a new one early 2024.” Professor Omoregie, who said he was part of the technical crew involved in the review of that initial one, said there was a lot of pruning down to accommodate some of the fears of the former president that it almost totally diluted its core value. “They were talking about guarantees that people had to guarantee when they took the facility. They even limited the amount that was to be drawn to a certain amount; there was nothing like upkeep of all of those things. President Tinubu didn’t think it was good enough, and he had to bring a new version. “I am sure even from outside the country now they will come and study sooner rather than later because, unlike many of the student loans that you have in America, the UK and all that, which makes them sceptical, this one is an interest-free loan. Maybe they should even use another word instead of calling it a loan. This is more like a grant; there is a moratorium that until you start working, nobody is going to bother you, and when you start working, nobody is going to ask you to pay with the bulk; rather, they would just take just a minute portion of your emolument. Everything will work out in such a way that you will not be burning out.” The post Nigeria’s NELFUND better than US, UK education loan models – UNIBEN VC appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Invest In Training, Boost Production To 3m/b Per Day, PETAN Urges Indigenous Oil Firms
item.description: The Petroleum Technology Association of Nigeria (PETAN) has urged indigenous oil and gas companies to invest in training young Nigerians and strengthening technical capacity to support the country’s ambition of producing three million barrels of crude oil per day. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, made the call at the association’s media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, warning that the transfer of oil and gas assets from international oil companies to indigenous operators had created an urgent need to train the next generation of industry professionals. He said Nigeria faced a widening gap between experienced oil and gas workers and younger professionals entering the industry, stressing that local operators must develop training programmes to sustain production and retain technical expertise. “We have a huge gap between those that are experienced in the industry versus age. Training is a very important aspect of our industry,” Ogunsanya said. PETAN Chairman, Wole Ogunsanya, while addressing journalists at a media roundtable in Lagos on Monday, October 26, 2026. He noted that many experienced Nigerian professionals had received their training through multinational companies, including Shell, ExxonMobil, Chevron and TotalEnergies, often benefiting from international placements and technical development programmes. However, he questioned whether similar opportunities would remain available as international operators divested some of their onshore, swamp and shallow-water assets. “Now we are divesting the assets. We are selling the assets to indigenous companies. Almost 100 per cent of the assets on land, in the swamp and shallow waters are owned by Nigerian indigenous companies. “Who is going to train the Nigerians? The new generation of Nigerians are coming behind to take over and operate those assets and work for these companies successfully,” he said. Training Centre Ogunsanya said Nigeria had sufficient human resources to develop its oil and gas industry, but needed to do more to attract graduates and provide them with practical skills. “The issue is not that we don’t have Nigerian young educated graduates that can come into the industry. The issue is how do we encourage these young educated Nigerian graduates to look into the oil and gas industry?” he asked. He said the industry required professionals with practical experience in drilling, pipeline installation, fabrication, welding and offshore operations, adding that training must prepare young Nigerians for the physical and technical demands of the sector. Ogunsanya disclosed that PETAN recruited nearly 100 engineers every two years through its internship programme, placing them in member companies for practical training. “After two years, PETAN members absorb over 60 per cent of these guys because that’s how good the training that we’re giving them is,” he said. item.title: Nigeria needs 9% annual growth to reduce poverty – Soludo
item.description: Governor Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra says Nigeria needs an annual economic growth of at least nine per cent to significantly reduce poverty and create jobs. He made the assertion at the Nigerian Economic Summit 32 (NES32) with the theme “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity” in Abuja on Monday. He said that Nigeria’s current growth rate of about four per cent remained inadequate to achieve rapid poverty reduction and employment generation. The governor also said that Nigeria would require an annual growth of at least 12 per cent to achieve a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2030 or 2040. He added that the country’s investment rate, estimated at 17 to 20 per cent, must rise significantly to support the required economic expansion. Soludo cautioned against being misled by large nominal spending figures, saying that consolidated public expenditure across all government levels amounted to less than one dollar per person daily. He stressed the need to channel national savings into productive investments, capable of expanding economic output, creating jobs and improving living standards. He called for stronger coordination between the federal government, states and local governments, noting that subnational authorities accounted for a substantial share of public spending. According to him, effective collaboration is essential to maximise the impact of government policies and investments across the country. Soludo cited Anambra’s free education programme, which covers kindergarten through secondary school, as an example of interventions delivering measurable social benefits. He said that the state had reduced its out-of-school children rate from 2.5 per cent to 0.25 per cent. He also cited a recent Oxford and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) report which reportedly placed Anambra’s multidimensional poverty rate at 9.6 per cent. Soludo said that reducing food prices required structural reforms to address post-harvest losses, which he put at about 43 per cent of agricultural output. He said that improving storage, transportation and distribution systems would help to move food from farms to urban markets and reduce consumer prices. The governor, therefore, urged governments to strengthen sectoral collaboration and mobilise investments to accelerate economic growth. Soludo also called for policies that encourage exports, develop domestic value chains and promote investment in sectors where Nigeria has competitive advantages. He emphasised that stronger private-sector participation and productive investments were essential to generating sustainable jobs and ensuring that economic growth benefitted more Nigerians. item.title: Nigeria’s Index Ebola Patient, Husband Evacuated To Switzerland – Pate
item.description: Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Ali Pate, on Monday confirmed that the first imported Ebola virus disease case in the country has been flown out of the country to Switzerland. Pate made the confirmation on his X handle, stating that the index patient, who has clinically improved, is stable and conscious, was evacuated along with her husband, who remained asymptomatic. He wrote: “I confirm that, with my approval, earlier this morning, the index case for Nigeria’s first imported Ebola virus disease departed Abuja for Switzerland. The index patient was clinically much improved, stable, conscious, communicating, and her clinical laboratory test results closing towards baseline. He, however, stated that her improvements do not mean she is not infectious, stating that strict protocols were put in place before her evacuation. “This does not mean she is not still infectious, hence the strict protocols in place. The patient was evacuated along with her spouse who has remained asymptomatic. ‘I thank all the various clinical staff for the high quality care they provided the patient as well as the public health personnel who ensured the evacuation was carried out in line with best public health measures for such evacuations. “We will provide further updates later this afternoon after the patient and her spouse lands successfully in their destination. “All public health measures are continuing to ensure successful containment of the imported virus. “I urge Nigerians to remain vigilant and rely on information from credible sources”, Pate said. The development came after the Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), on Sunday, said that the number of contacts linked to the index case of Ebola recorded in October 2026 had risen to 53. The agency said the contacts comprise health workers as well as the domestic staff and spouse of the patient diagnosed with the disease. The NCDC, in its Ebola Disease Situation Report, said that a newly suspected case was reported by Rivers State on October 23, but laboratory results returned negative for Ebola disease. “Fifty-three contacts linked to the index case have so far been identified, categorized and followed up. Contacts listed include healthcare workers, domestic staff and spouse,” the report dated October 24, 2026, partly read. Giving a background on the index case, it said the patient is a 42-year-old woman who returned from Uganda through Addis Ababa on October 3, 2026, via an international flight to Abuja, Nigeria. The agency said she became symptomatic four days later and presented to a private health facility on October 10, and another on October 11. “She presented to another private facility on the 11th of October 2026, where she was admitted.
